Hello, world: a small space for ideas

A first entry in my notebook, with a few photographs, a sample table, and room for ideas to grow.

YC
Yuqiao Chen

October 4, 2026 · 2 min read

Welcome to my little corner of the internet. Alongside my research projects, this blog is a place for working notes, things I am learning, and occasional moments away from the screen.

A template, for now. This is a sample post to demonstrate the blog layout. The photographs are illustrative stock images, and the table below contains made-up data, not research results or a record of my travels.

A notebook in the open

Some ideas are easier to understand when written down. I hope to use this space for research reflections, practical implementation notes, and questions I want to revisit later.

A post does not have to be a polished paper. It can be a small observation, a useful diagram, or an explanation that finally made something click.

Putting observations in a table

Here is a simple Markdown table. All values are fictional, included only to show formatting.

Example approach Tasks completed Average steps Note
Baseline 12 / 20 8.4 Illustrative only
With memory 15 / 20 7.1 Illustrative only
With structured feedback 16 / 20 6.8 Illustrative only

When sharing real results, I would also include the evaluation setup, data provenance, uncertainty, and limitations. A table is a starting point for an explanation.

A small code example

Fenced code blocks work too:

def record_observation(question, evidence):
    return {
        "question": question,
        "evidence": evidence,
        "next_step": "Design a small, testable experiment",
    }

Things to come back to

  • What makes an agent’s experience useful for a future task?
  • How can we make intermediate decisions easier to inspect?
  • What is the smallest experiment that could disprove an idea?

Thanks for reading. You can find my current work on the projects page, or get in touch.
